title: Roxas, Quirino & Magsaysay
subtitle: Three presidents, one continuous problem.
objectives: Describe the Roxas, Quirino and Magsaysay administrations
Compare how each handled corruption and unrest
Explain why Magsaysay is remembered as he is
Assess the record of the early republic

cards.title: Rebuilding, scandal, and a change of tone
cards.text: The first decade of the republic ran through three very different men and one continuous problem.

cards.title: 1946 to 1948: independence and its price
cards.text: He led the country into independence and died in office.
points: **Accepted the Bell Trade Act** and the bases agreement.
**Granted amnesty** to those accused of collaboration.
**Faced the growing Huk rebellion.**
**Died of a heart attack in 1948**, at Clark Field.

cards.title: 1948 to 1953: rebuilding under a cloud
cards.text: Real reconstruction happened. So did a reputation for corruption.
points: **Infrastructure and the economy** recovered somewhat.
**Negotiated with the Huks**, without lasting success.
**Accusations of overspending and graft** dominated his image.
**The 1949 election** was widely seen as fraudulent.

cards.title: Six presidents, one fact each
cards.text: Tap through. The last button is the thread running under all of them.

question.text: Which president led the country into independence in 1946?
question.explain: Manuel Roxas, who died in office in 1948.

cards.title: The golden arinola, and why reputation sticks
cards.text: Quirino was accused of buying a gold chamber pot. The story was almost certainly false and it defined him anyway.
points: **Repeated often enough**, it became the thing people knew.
**It was political attack**, not reporting.
**He lost heavily in 1953.**
**A reminder:** check whether a famous story was ever true.

cards.title: 1953 to 1957: the change of tone
cards.text: He won on a promise to make government reachable, and largely kept it.
points: **Opened Malacañang** to ordinary visitors.
**Ended the Huk rebellion** with force and reform together.
**Pushed resettlement** for surrendered rebels.
**Died in a plane crash in 1957**, still in office.

question.text: Magsaysay ended the Huk rebellion using military force alone.
question.explain: He combined military pressure with amnesty, land and an end to army abuses. Force alone had already failed.

cards.title: Two presidents and two aircraft
cards.text: The early republic lost two leaders in ways that shaped what came next.
points: **Roxas died at Clark Field** in 1948, after a speech.
**Magsaysay died in a crash** on Mount Manunggal in 1957.
**Both were in office**, both successions were sudden.
**Continuity is fragile** when it rests on one person.

options: making government reachable and ending the Huk rebellion
question.explain: Accessibility plus the combined force-and-reform approach.

cards.title: The office, not the man
cards.alt: An empty official office with a heavy wooden desk, an empty leather chair and a blank nameplate
cards.text: Three presidents in seven years. Two died while holding it.

cards.title: Reputation is built on what people can see
cards.text: Magsaysay's open-door policy was partly substance and partly a very good decision about visibility.
points: **People judge** what they can observe.
**He let them observe a lot.**
**Quirino's achievements** were real and invisible.
**Both things are true at once.**

terms.def: Using public office for private gain.
Moving families to new farmland, used with surrendered rebels.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Roxas led into independence and died in 1948.
Quirino rebuilt, and was defined by corruption accusations.
Magsaysay ended the rebellion with force and reform together.
Two of the three died in office, both suddenly.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 8 Social Studies. Three administrations compared on how each handled the same two pressures, corruption and rural unrest, which gives the decade a shape rather than a sequence. The Quirino card does real work beyond the syllabus: the golden arinola story was almost certainly untrue and defined him anyway, which is a transferable lesson about checking whether a famous story was ever verified. Magsaysay's reputation is given honestly as both genuine achievement and a very effective decision about visibility, with Quirino's real and invisible reconstruction set beside it.
discussion: Why did force alone fail against the Huks?
Was the golden arinola story true, and does that matter?
Why is Quirino remembered worse than his record?
extension: Look up whether the arinola story was ever substantiated.
Compare what each of the three actually built.
misconceptions: That Magsaysay used only military force.
That a famous story must be true.
